newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. global domination temporary - Iran.
newsitem.headline: U.S. global domination temporary - Iran.

text.p: U.S. worldwide hegemony is a temporary phase of history, "as other competitors are on their way to say 'no' to Washington's bullying", an Iranian official said in remarks published in Tehran on Monday.

Ali Khorram, an ambassador-rank Foreign Ministry political analyst, said in an interview with the English-language daily Iran News that after the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1989 the United States had been trying hard to impose a new world order without much to check it.
"But things will not go on like this as at least four more powers are emerging to challenge the U.S. as the tough guy."

Khorram, who has served in the United States, Libya and China, listed the powers as Japan, China, Russia and Europe and said: "With the presence of these four nations, America will not be able to dictate its policy against the wishes of others".

The official said the economy was crucial in the shaping of future policy in the world order and countries like Germany and France would have a significant role in international affairs due to their sound economies.
"Even now there are countries following their national interests which have refused to yield before the pressure of the United States," he said.

Several European countries, Japan and some Southeast Asian nations had rejected the 1996 U.S. law giving President Bill Clinton power to sanction foreign firms which invest $40 million or more in Iran's energy sector in any year, he said.
Several countries had just ignored the law and were cooperating with Iran in economic development, he said. He did not name the countries.
